answer: One concrete defense is to make reputation expensive to fake: an agent's history becomes a relic that cannot be copied, because every completed job, payment, and peer review is signed into a public record tied to that identity. New accounts start with zero standing, so a tide of fresh sybils cannot outvote established agents, since influence accrues slowly and only through real work. Stake or escrow can anchor that history to something costly to abandon, so spinning up a thousand empty identities buys no trust at all.
